newsitem.title: USA: US March S&P 500 ends down in sync with tech slump.
newsitem.headline: US March S&P 500 ends down in sync with tech slump.

text.p: U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended moderately lower, unable to shake off weak technology stocks.
March slipped as low as 786.50 after hitting a two-week high earlier. Traders tied the failure to followthrough from Friday's gains to a sluggish Treasury bond tone and the limp tech sector.

"We saw a lot of selling late after the tech sector couldn't recover at all," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "Not a bad comeback from the lows, but I still think any rallies tomorrow will be met by selling."
Tech losses were tied to a warning from computer networking company 3Com Corp that its third-quarter results would be below most analysts' estimates.
For March S&Ps, it was the fourth rejection of the 796.00 area since the record high was achieved on January 23.
One trader said the failure at that level suggested the market was uncomfortable in this record-high territory and could correct lower.
"But you've got to believe if we ever print 97-even there's got to be huge stops and then we'll see 800.00," he said.
Another trader said a near-term challenge of 800.00 was stymied by Monday's failure after Friday's rally.
"It's not looking like we're going to be moving that way soon," he said. "We might have blown it for a little while."

He pegged the next level of support at 785.80 to 786.00, with the next zone at 783.00, he said. Monday's session high of 796.95 and a gap in liquidity from 793.40 to 793.60 should be resistance on Tuesday, he said.
The old two-week high at 796.60 should also be a cap for gains, the trader said.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were down 6.30 at 788.05, Value Lines were 5.50 lower at 702.50, NYSE Composites were 3.15 lower at 413.05, Nikkeis were 310 higher at 18,110, Midcap 400s were down 2.70 at 263.10 and Nasdaq 100s were down 32.20 at 874.50.
